en: Sutta Nipāta 5.10 Todeyya-māṇava-pucchā “In whom sensual desires do not dwell, ... [the rest of the verse follows] ...”
and who has crossed over all doubt— "
“In that which desires do not dwell,” said the Blessed One to Todeyya.
For one in whom craving no longer exists,
who has crossed over all doubt—
there is for him no further liberation.
“Is he one who is without hope yet still hopeful,
or one who possesses wisdom yet fashions his own wisdom?
O Sakka, how may I truly know such a sage?”
"Explain that to me, O All-Seeing One.
"He is without longing and does not long for anything;
he possesses wisdom and does not fashion wisdom through mere conceptualization."
"Thus, Todeyya, know the sage to be one who possesses nothing and is unattached to sensual existence.
The ninth inquiry of the young brahmin Todeyya.
